entries.answer: A past paper is a previous year's exam, and using real ones is the most reliable preparation available because they show the actual format rather than a guess at it. They also reveal weighting, since a topic that appears every year is worth more time than a large section of the syllabus does. The mistake is treating them as tests rather than as information, so people sit one, score badly, and stop. Sitting under time pressure is worth doing, but reading where the marks actually go is worth more.

patterns: how to review a mock exam
entries.answer: A mock exam is a practice paper sat under real conditions, and its value is almost entirely in what happens afterwards. The score matters less than the review, and a review means finding out why each wrong answer was wrong rather than merely that it was. A mock sat without a proper review is close to worthless, and it can be actively misleading because it produces a false sense of readiness. Two or three well-reviewed mocks are worth more than a full set of unanswered ones.

patterns: is a syllabus a reading list
how to use a syllabus to revise
entries.answer: A syllabus is the list of what an exam covers, and its purpose is to let you allocate time, so it is a scheduling document rather than a reading list. The weighting matters as much as the list, because a three-mark topic and a twelve-mark one are not the same amount of work. A common and expensive mistake is covering everything once rather than going deep on what is actually asked, and the fix is to read the mark scheme first, which usually describes the shape of the answer.

patterns: should you read the mark scheme
entries.answer: A mark scheme is the examiner's breakdown of how an answer is credited, and it is the most underused document in any exam. It shows that the question is marked against specific points rather than for fluency, and it reveals the difference between an answer that is right and an answer that earns the marks. Many students lose marks for a correct idea expressed in the wrong form, which is visible in the scheme and invisible in the textbook.

patterns: is cramming better than spaced study
entries.answer: Cramming is putting all the revision into the shortest possible time, and the research is consistent that it works better than nothing while being worse than spaced study over the same total hours. What it does well is retrieval of facts, surface names and figures, which is often exactly what a short-answer question asks. What it does badly is retention afterwards, and it reliably produces a spike during the exam and a drop the week after. It is a legitimate tool for a specific kind of short test and a poor substitute for a term.
